source.title: How Post-Training Reshapes LLMs: A Mechanistic View on Knowledge, Truthfulness, Refusal, and Confidence
source.authors: Hongzhe Du; Weikai Li; Min Cai; Karim Saraipour; Zimin Zhang; Himabindu Lakkaraju; Yizhou Sun; Shichang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures entropy neurons and post-training effects on knowledge, truthfulness, refusal, and confidence. It does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether neurons are polysemantic.
record.gate_note: The paper's entropy-neuron findings concern a different property of neurons, not polysemanticity. They are recorded as findings that fit none of the claim versions; cited work and model/layer choices are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper compares base and post-trained LLMs on knowledge storage, truthfulness and refusal directions, and entropy neurons. It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, nor superposition, architecture effects or measurement choices. Polysemanticity is not tested. Strictly the paper only cites polysemanticity work (e.g. Templeton et al.), so 'cites_only' would also fit; the record's 'discusses' is kept as a near-equivalent.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as far as it goes. The authors also conclude that post-training preserves knowledge-storage locations and truthfulness directions, adapts knowledge representations while adding new ones, and changes the refusal direction, which then transfers poorly forward.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies post-training effects on knowledge, truthfulness, refusal, and confidence; it does not apply a method for identifying or testing polysemantic neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-layer entropy neurons largely overlap between base and post-trained models (8–10 of 10 in Table 18; 10/10 for Llama-2-13B). Ratio differences are under 1% of the mean ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entropy neurons and their weight-norm/LogitVar properties are largely preserved through post-training in the tested 7–13B models.

record.problems: The paper does not measure polysemanticity or evaluate whether individual neurons have coherent or mixed input-related functions. The entropy-neuron results are reported for selected final-layer candidates and do not establish anything about polysemanticity.

untested.parts: All; no measure of neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts.
All; post-training is not analysed for its effect on polysemanticity.

record.verdict_notes: No bearing on any polysemanticity version. The rows are properly unlinked and the study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Whether vision-model neurons respond to unrelated image inputs.
Whether a large share of transformer MLP neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Whether polysemanticity varies with architecture, activation, or regularization, or can be reduced without a large performance loss.
Whether apparent mixed neuron responses are actually a shared feature or related jobs.
Whether polysemanticity depends on the activation range examined or the explanation-scoring method.
